measurements.name: lens_mm
measurements.method: Three conditions together: (1) the rotation-corrected focus of expansion, from the template-tracked rail post (scale and position) after removing the far-skyline drift, is 397 px above the image centre at (343,563); (2) the background mullion converges at dx/dy=-0.044 at x=1045, measured on 21 frames; (3) the handrail slope is +0.024. These give f*tan(pitch)=397 px, and a horizontal eye-level dolly with roll ~+1 deg comes out at 47-59 mm. Image scale ratios alone cannot fix the lens.

measurements.name: face_box_physical_size
measurements.method: Detector box compared with crown-to-chin measured on f1, f41, f111 and f148 (ratio 0.93-1.00); MMD 1.58 m girl head of 0.235 m. Everything in metres scales with this value.

measurements.name: camera_to_DS_face_distance_f1
measurements.method: f_px*0.23/w with w corrected to 410 px. The raw 390 px box is ~5% narrow because the head is yawed 14 deg. The correction is chosen so that the rail post's scale track and the face scale agree over f40-69 (least coefficient of variation, post plane 0.12 m in front of the face).

measurements.name: camera_to_DS_face_distance_f148
measurements.method: f_px*0.23/w with the face box smoothed by loess and a 5th-order fit of depth over time (w~834 px)

measurements.name: dolly_travel
measurements.method: Camera centres back-projected from the smoothed face-box centre and size with a fixed head point and the measured orientation

measurements.name: camera_height_rel_DS_face_point
measurements.method: The horizon (rotation-corrected focus of expansion, y=563 px) passes through DS's eyes; confirmed by overlaying the horizon on f1, f37, f73, f109 and f145

measurements.name: camera_height_above_rail_top
measurements.method: Least-squares fit of the projected rail line to the detected rail highlight line (y at x=540 and slope) over f1-99, 5 px rms

measurements.name: pitch
measurements.method: Starting pitch = atan(397/f_px). The tilt-up comes from NCC tracking of the top-left skyline patch (content moves down 80 px by f89) and is extrapolated at 1 px/frame afterwards.

measurements.name: roll
measurements.method: Rail image slope stays at 1.2-1.8 deg through f1-99 while DS rotates +2.4 deg, so DS's rotation is her body, not the camera. The rail slope is split into roll and perspective so that it agrees with the mullion convergence.

measurements.name: yaw
measurements.value: camera axis along -Y, perpendicular to the rail (rail yaw fit -1.4 +- 1.5)
measurements.method: Rail line fit with free yaw versus yaw fixed at 0 gives the same 5 px rms

measurements.name: rail_relation_to_face_point
measurements.value: axis y=F+0.079 toward camera; highlight 0.415 below F; tube top ~0.385 below F
measurements.method: Least-squares fit of a horizontal line along X projected through the camera keys against the per-frame rail highlight line from a brute-force gradient line search, f1-99

measurements.name: rail_post_position
measurements.value: x=+0.18 (DS's right), in the rail plane, cap 0.455 below F
measurements.method: Triangulated from the scaled template track of the bottle post, f1-69 (NCC>0.87); 21 px rms because DS's own sideways drift is folded into the camera

measurements.name: background_window_mullion

measurements.name: background_guests

open_issues: The lens is only loosely constrained (40-65 mm). All scale and parallax ratios are the same for any lens, so 50 mm rests on a horizontal eye-level dolly plus noisy convergence of a single background mullion and the rail slope. If the consolidator prefers another lens, scale every C-F offset by lens/50 and set the pitch to -atan(397/(lens/36*1920)).

The 0.17 m face-box prior in the task does not fit the image: the detector box is about crown-to-chin, ~0.23 m. Every metric distance in this fragment (camera offsets, rail 0.385 m below F, background depths) scales linearly with this choice and with the user's actual MMD head size.

The world numbers assume Ybal=8.0 and zbal=3.5 (F=[0,-8,4.95]). The architecture specialist must re-anchor by translating every CAM_Shot1 location and target and the DOF focus by (F_new - F). The rail spec should keep the rail top 0.385 m below F and the rail axis 0.08 m toward the camera from F. That puts the rail top at zbal+1.065, so a 1.58 m upright MMD DS (face point ~1.42 m) needs a 0.03 m lift or a 0.03 m lower rail and camera.

In the original, DS herself drifts ~3 cm to screen-right (f1-50), sinks ~4 cm (f100-148) and rolls +2.4 deg. The keys absorb the translations so a static head matches the anchors, at the cost of up to ~20-45 px sideways error on the sharp rail post in f1-69. The horizontal rail itself is unaffected.

After f89 the far skyline is hidden, so the camera tilt-up there (1 px/frame, ending 3.0 deg total) is extrapolated. Tracks of the late-shot left and right edges are polluted by DS's hair and moving guests.

The camera in shot 1 hangs over the pit void outside the balustrade, while a blurred foreground crowd head appears at the lower left in f1-50. That head cannot be built consistently; it is left out (a camera-parented card is optional).
The original timing (motion on only 3 of 5 frames) is not reproduced by the smooth keys. A global time remap with holds would be needed for frame-exact comparison in all shots.

Shot 2 is filmed from just behind DS on the same balcony. The shot-2 solver should confirm that DS faces +Y at [0,-8.0,~4.95] with the rail 0.08 m in front of her face point. A conflict would mean the shot-1 rail relation is a per-shot cheat.
